title: Frontend entry systemdesign spa routing
question: How would you design basic client-side routing for a small single-page app with a handful of pages, like Home, Profile, and Settings?
idealAnswer:
Map URL paths to components so the browser's URL bar reflects the current view, using the History API (pushState/replaceState) rather than only changing state in memory

Support browser back/forward buttons correctly by listening for popstate, so navigation feels native rather than breaking the browser's expected behavior

Handle direct loads and refreshes of non-root URLs (e.g. /settings) correctly, this usually requires server or static-host configuration to serve the app shell for any path, not just the router changing on the client

Consider code-splitting each route so the JS for Settings isn't downloaded until the user actually navigates there, keeping the initial load light

Think through what happens for routes that don't match anything (a 404/not-found view) and routes that require auth (redirecting unauthenticated users)

Preserve scroll position appropriately, e.g. resetting scroll on navigation to a new page but restoring it when the user goes back
